text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALL newspapers lead with Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's lashing out at "rogue" currency speculators and "anarchists" who have caused a currency crisis in Southeast Asia.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said Malaysia may submit a proposal for a much-required review of the Universal Declaration on Human Rights. He said the declaration proclaimed 50 years ago was no longer suitable.
-- Malaysia Mining Corp gets 34 million ringgit contract to refurbish Malaysian army's 150 Condor armoured personnel carriers.
-- The DRB-Hicom group will spend between 500 million and one billion ringgit to manufacture military vehicles and equipment, the Chief Minister of Malacca state, Abu Zahar Isnin said.

-- Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd is looking for options to reduce its stake in independent television station, TV3, its chairman Khalid Ahmad said. He said MRCB could sell off stake in lots of two percent or bigger blocks of 10 percent. "We may retain the maximum 75 percent or go down to 60 percent," Khalid said. TV3 is undergoing a restructuring under which MRCB is injecting its stake in New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd into the television company.

-- The Sabah state government has set January 1, next year as the target date for completion of the privatisation of Sabah Elecrtricity Board. State-controlled but listed Tenaga Nasional Bhd will head a consortium to take over the entity.

-- The recently listed aviation services provider Transmile Group Bhd is expected to undergo a restructuring under which it will sell 30 of its 61 percent stake in subsidiary Transmile Air Services Sdn Bhd to shipping and transportation firm Konsortium Perkapalan Bhd. Transmile will also take up a 30 percent stake in state run courier services Pos Laju.
